title: SharePoint: find information and get answers from Lists in Knowledge Agent
summary: Hold: the spending-policy path omits the choice of Advanced work in SharePoint, and the guidance still recommends preview availability settings whose documented retirement date has passed. Learn already describes included list-question capabilities and relevant permission and sensitivity-label rules, so the briefing overstates what remains unknown.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans relevant information, matching items and answers from Microsoft Lists using Knowledge Agent.
claims.quote: Users will be able to find relevant information, matching items and get answers from Microsoft Lists using Knowledge Agent.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits content discovery from covered SharePoint sites in organization-wide search and Copilot responses.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses while those reviews are taking place.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level control.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires Copilot licensing and SharePoint Advanced Management availability.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: By default only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Delegation of Restricted Content Discovery management to site administrators is a separate tenant setting.
claims.quote: If you want site administrators to manage the setting for their own sites, enable delegation by using the following PowerShell command: Set-SPOTenant -DelegateRestrictedContentDiscoverabilityManagement $true

claims.claim: The site restriction path is SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables the site restriction.
claims.quote: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: The documented preview tenant opt-out command is Set-SPOTenant -KnowledgeAgentScope NoSites.
claims.quote: Turn off Copilot in SharePoint for the tenant: Set-SPOTenant -KnowledgeAgentScope NoSites

claims.claim: No tenant admin UI counterpart to the historical KnowledgeAgentScope preview control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot in SharePoint tenant availability admin center KnowledgeAgentScope Site AI settings. Read get-started, Restricted Content Discovery and configure-Copilot-admin-center excerpts; found site controls, not a tenant KnowledgeAgentScope UI.

claims.claim: Other KnowledgeAgentScope values are AllSites, IncludeSelectedSites and ExcludeSelectedSites.
claims.quote: AllSites: Copilot in SharePoint is available on all sites. IncludeSelectedSites: Copilot in SharePoint is available only on sites specified in KnowledgeAgentSelectedSitesList.

claims.quote: After November 1, 2026, manage availability by using Site AI settings and Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Learn's preview PowerShell guidance tells multigeo tenants to run the script in each geo.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; controls[2].note; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Advanced work requires usage-based billing through a spending policy and consumes Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: To use advanced capabilities or to work at greater scale, users need usage-based billing enabled through a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center and available Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Copilot asks the user to approve credit use before continuing into advanced work.
claims.quote: When a prompt requires an advanced capability, or crosses the threshold of working at scale, Copilot asks the user to approve credit use before continuing.

claims.claim: Copilot warns users when 20% of the monthly credit limit remains.
claims.quote: When 20% of the monthly credit limit remains, Copilot notifies the user that usage-based features pause until the next month when the limit is reached.

claims.claim: Learn says usage-based features pause until the next month when the monthly credit limit is reached.
claims.quote: When 20% of the monthly credit limit remains, Copilot notifies the user that usage-based features pause until the next month when the limit is reached.
claims.fix: Keep the attribution to the SharePoint page, but add: 'The general monitoring documentation qualifies per-user limits: a running task that exceeds a group policy's per-user limit can complete without interruption.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending.

claims.claim: Existing spending policies might automatically include new services when Allow new agents and services as they become available is enabled.
claims.quote: Existing cost management policies might automatically include newly available services if the Allow new agents and services as they become available option is turned on for the policy.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost management > Add spending policy > Limits and alerts is the route for a policy covering advanced SharePoint work.
claims.quote: Under Access scope, choose whether the policy applies to all users or to specific security groups. Under Agents and services, select Advanced work in SharePoint. Set Limits and alerts for the policy, choose a Billing method, then review and add the policy.
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].ui.path and its table path with 'Copilot > Cost management > Add spending policy > Access scope > Agents and services > Advanced work in SharePoint > Limits and alerts'. The service selection is a required choice, not a heading that can be omitted.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates spending-policy limits through periodLimit and perUserLimit.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b; The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: The licence assignment path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign, then select Save changes.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the selected user licence.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Licence assignment requires at least the License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Administrators can review Copilot Credit usage in Cost management by spending policy, user and service.
claims.quote: The Consumption tab provides reporting experiences for copilot credit usage by: Spending policy; User; Group; Agent; Service.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending for this monitoring statement; the SharePoint get-started page does not document these reporting views.

claims.claim: The licensing model for this list-information retrieval change is mixed.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not say how sensitivity labels apply to Copilot answers from lists.

claims.claim: The action rating is prepare despite documented no-opt-in rollout, a medium risk rating and available site controls.
claims.quote: action: prepare; risk: medium; no opt-in step is required; general availability begins rolling out on 30 September 2026; Turn on Restricted Content Discovery for sites that need review.
claims.fix: Set action to 'act-now': on the 22 November 2026 run, the documented no-opt-in rollout started within about 60 days, risk is medium and site controls are available.
